cim: Optimizing penetration testing workflows with in-house artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Optimizing penetration testing workflows with in-house artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Penetration testing demand is rising due to evolving regulatory requirements and security standards, yet many firms struggle to keep pace due to a shortage of experienced personnel and time-consuming manual documentation processes, based on information published by Bleeping Computer.

To address these inefficiencies, security firms are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to automate administrative tasks. Research indicates that while actual testing accounts for 50% of an engagement, documentation and review processes consume a significant portion of remaining billable hours. By integrating AI, firms can automate the drafting of findings, normalize scanner outputs from tools like Burp Suite and Nessus, and ensure consistency across reports.

A critical aspect of this transition is maintaining data sovereignty. Platforms such as PentestPad allow organizations to deploy language models within their own infrastructure, ensuring that sensitive client vulnerabilities remain secure. This approach enables testers to focus on high-value activities like exploit validation while the AI handles report formatting and executive summary generation.

By tracking metrics such as documentation-to-testing ratios and project delivery timelines, firms can quantify productivity gains. Implementing these workflows helps teams manage increased workloads without compromising the quality or security of their assessments, ultimately allowing for more efficient project management and faster client delivery cycles.
